Falcke, H., Holbrook, S., Clenahan, I., Lopez Carretero, A., Sanalan, T., Brinkmann, T., Roth, J., Zerger, B., Roudier, S. and Delgado Sancho, L. (2017). Best Available Techniques (BAT) Reference Document for the Production of Large Volume Organic Chemicals. Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU (Integrated Pollution Prevention and Control). JRC Science for Policy Report JRC109279, EUR 28882 EN. Luxembourg: Publications Office of the European Union. ISBN 978-92-79-76589-6, doi:10.2760/77304.

Targeted pass of a 693-page BREF (printed pages 1-653; PDF page = printed + 38 up to p.~330, + 37 after). Locators are PRINTED page numbers. Loaded: per-product energy use from the "Energy consumption" sections - steam cracking world-average SEC and furnace thermal input (Ch.3), aromatics BB1-BB3 utilities (Table 4.3), ethylbenzene, EB-dehydrogenation styrene and SMPO utilities (Sect. 5.3.5), formaldehyde silver/oxide electricity, methanol use and steam export (Table 6.10), EO feed ratios and CO2 by-product (Table 7.6, Sect. 7.3.6.1), phenol steam/electricity (Table 8.5), VCM steam/fuel/electricity (Table 11.13), H2O2 total net energy (Table 12.5), Sumitomo HCl oxidation (emerging, Sect. 11.5.2), and three Ch.2 summary boxes with numbers (acrylonitrile, FAME biodiesel, bioethanol). Not loaded: ethanolamines and TDI/MDI (no energy numbers printed), all BAT-AELs and pollutant data, water, waste; techniques without numbers (cracker heat integration, burner location, fractionation configuration, flameless combustion etc.). The BREF prints no investment or operating cost figures for any process or technique, so there are no capex/opex rows. Emerging techniques (OCM, metathesis, benzene from methane, DMO glycol, direct phenol, phosgene-free isocyanates, direct H2O2) carry no numbers. No data for the gap/estimated chemicals archetypes (catalytic naphtha cracking, rotodynamic/electric cracking, adipic acid, N2O destruction) - adipic acid is only described qualitatively (p.22).

(1) Table 4.3 (aromatics) prints component minima/maxima from different plants that do not add to the totals (BB3 fuel max 3 960 kWh/t exceeds total max 2 854); row order is Total Max-Min, then Min-Max for components. (2) Energy in Sect. 5.3.5 is given in kWh for steam and fuel; heating-value basis never stated. (3) Table 8.5 (phenol) gives two rows from two references without saying which is which; recorded as case-1 and case-2. (4) Table 11.13 prints MWH/t. (5) The steam cracker 26 GJ/t ethylene is a reprinted world average (US EPA 2004), not EU data. (6) Table 12.5 does not state the H2O2 concentration basis of the total. (7) EO CO2 0.22-0.86 t/t is a stoichiometric maximum for 70-90 % selectivity, not measured emissions. (8) Formaldehyde Table 6.10 is reprinted from the 2003 LVOC BREF.
